Marcus Naukratius, It is truly terrible that Calidus sent you away, but I hope you arrive to the warm hearths I always imagine of quaint Brettanogh. Something has begun here, a movement among the right sort of people, against the usurper. Calidus knows only violence, and destruction. They fear him, as you have seen, but they also despise him. They know, like a dog with a bone, he will eat away at the idea of Rome until there's nothing left of it. I will restore the natural order that Lucius fought for all his life. Pax. Stability. Everything as it should be. For now we must find a little patience; prepare. Stones cast in Albion, dear Marcus, may have greater ripples than you might believe. It could stoke the fires of debate in the senate— the very people I must persuade. Proud Juliana waits for you still. Julia Augusta.

Defines the footprint of their Rival on the map; e.g. how many Islands they settle, and in which provinces they will be present. High ratings mean they take islands independently of your progress, and the availability of resource alternatives such as trade. These characters also unlock provinces independently of you, and settle there whenever they can. A low rating slows a Rival's expansion— they will adjust their expansion to new islands based on your rate of expansion. They only enter other provinces once you have.

Dear Marcia, I hope you are well, and that your journey to Albion was uneventful. I have heard no gossip pertaining to you, which means you've done well. Nevertheless, I implore you to be careful. Out in the wild, you may be out of sight but not out of mind.

In the meantime, rest assured: I have not given up on my claim. Already the malcontents flock to meet me in the temple of Minerva. Calidus' hold on the senate is feeble.
Once it is within my power, I will summon you back to Latium. In the meantime, I hope you can arrange yourself comfortably in your new home. I am counting on you. Perhaps by the time you receive this, you will already be ruling respectable city in the cold, unruly north. Cura ut valeas. Julia Augusta.

Ave, Praetor I bear the responsibility for sending forth the Classis Albionis, so I must also bear the responsibility for its loss. My apologies for infringing upon your imperium, Governor. I simply felt passionate, as a Roman man, that something had to be done about the province of Albion. I am given to understand that the province is traditionally neglected, overrun as it is by savages and barbarians. With the total defeat of the Classis Albionis, I begin to see why. It is a shame the Senate and the Emperor care so little for the state of the province. One of my own family was lost in the battle, you know. No matter. The fight in Albion continues, I'm sure. To that end, I have dispatched a loyal navarch, veteran of the Albionic conquest. His experience ought to prove useful if you plan on doing anything about your province's barbarian problem. I trust you will do right by us all; by the Eternal City, by Jupiter, by all Romans everywhere. Ave atque vale, Primus Cornelius Albionicus

At that time my sister Caecilia served at the great temple of Ambrosia. A day before we were due to meet, I saw a cloud that was extending like a vine, growing tendrils in every direction.

As I watched, the walls started shaking so violently that everything in the room was turned upside down. We ran outside, yelling, the servants covering their heads, for some of the statues in the garden had started toppling down.

There we saw that the cloud advanced, just as the sea seemed to retreat from it, leaving the fish stranded in its wake.

Darkness descended, a starless night full of choking black smoke. Ashes fell like snow, and all I could see henceforth was the glint of distant fires...

Procurator Corvinus is the Emperor's watchful eye in Albion. Saddled with the difficult job of holding fort at the edge of the known world, Corvinus is conflicted between escaping almost anywhere else and seeing out his days in the place he loves to hate. His duties include monitoring the performance of local Governors while providing them a fiscal safety net, relaying imperial instructions, and imprisoning Celtic miscreants. Corvinus is a man of great integrity and professionalism, and though understandably cautious at first, is bound to thaw over time.

You stand tall, and hold forth upon the topic of your own majesty. Shining, cities, glorious villas, marble and mosaics. A well-greased loom that weaves labour into luxury. A world run not by the rule of violence for violence. The Legate cracks a smile. "Well, not your bloody violence, I suppose. Nice for them that can get it. But where'd you think all this comes from, eh?" He gestures around at Syracus' villa. "Who'd you think built this? And where'dya think they came from? It's blood all the way down, Governor dearest, and blood's still blood even if you're not the one sheddin' it. You stylus-pusher types, you and Syracus, you think you're above it all? The things I've seen in the name of civilization..." The venom in his voice is undeniable, even to the most sycophantic in the audience. Realising he's said too much, the Legate coughs, waves you away, and abruptly changes the subject to the olive groves of Kyklopia. You got a clue!

An easy sinecure, Lucius hoped, to keep his enemy close and his ambitions under control.
Neferneru is not a man so easily stopped. Those who invite him into their domain should expect a challenge. Once opened, the maw of the Kashtan lion is not easily closed.

Primus, the big man of house Cornelia, has pestered the Senate to "put an end to Albionic barbarism once and for all". I'm, um, not sure they remembered you're the Governor there? They've sent a whole fleet, the Classis Albionis, to go shoot anything that looks vaguely barbarian-shaped. So you're going to have to deal with all that. Hopefully this gets here before they do! Oh and, that boy you're looking for, Flavius? I hear he's been making a name for himself in the navy, lately. I'm no oracle, but that seems a bit ominous to me. Sorry! Full acccount of events leading to victory. Gaius Titanius Naso and household reached Whitecliff at the turning of the year.
Bout of illness kept him from speaking to public often, wife Titania helped pass on orders. Probably gout — journey to Albion did not improve his health.
Shortly after imperial visit, Titanius contracted marsh fever. Knew it was going to kill him, after ambush, risk of another attack was high. Had to involve and warn household.
Titanius died of fever. Same night, Celts rushed settlement full force, before legion could take up positions. Titania rallied household and led defence. Servants fought for master and mistress they loved. Crushed rebels. Regret to say legion played no part in victory.
Post Scriptum: Titanius fond of wife, would not want her punished.

Manx Anctius is a local tribal leader in Albion. The tribe has a history of good Roman relations and Manx welcomes Roman Governorship of the province. It turns out that under the previous Emperor, promises were made to Manx in return for his loyalty, that have not yet been fulfilled. Exposed, his once-proud tribe of expert horse breeders has been bullied and harassed, suffering humiliation at the hands of staunch anti-imperialist tribes, notably Voada and the Scathach. Jittery and unreliable at first, Manx's strengths emerge as you come to know him.

Julia Augusta is the loving wife of Lucius Augustus Florianus. She is also a savvy political operator connected by birth to Latium's most famous son, her father, Emperor Servius. Calm, charming, and pleasant, Julia seeks pragmatic solutions and has none of her husband's errant temper. She seeks to strengthen diplomatic ties to the outmost edges of the empire and sees war as a last resort. With her birth status comes a certain obliviousness towards the fate of slaves and those belonging to the lower classes, her political goals aimed at preserving the future of the empire as a whole. She intends to do all that she can to save the Pax Romana and turn the Eternal City into a capital of culture.

Voada is the face of the Celtic rebellion. The Queen of the Scathach, a tribe once famed for its iron mines, rails against the obliteration of Celtic customs. She wants to send the Romans back to the sea, unable to forget the incident that deprived her of her mines, her home and her son. A warrior all her days, she reveres the Celtic gods and sees war as the only way to unite her people, and preserve the old ways. Despite the whipscars on her back, or because of them, Voada is swift to repel any Romans that wander into her territory. The one deep, dark fear that keeps her awake at night is that her own people could forsake her – that they would bury their own songs and traditions, choosing to become Roman instead.

Senators guzzle amphorae of wine-dark wine, urged on by magistrates and merchants between mouthfuls of Iberian ham and Gaulish dormice, served at command by a battalion of slaves, men and women of every province, each one bound by a chain of gold. Trade Routes are an important part of a growing empire. Creating trade route are useful to automatically transfer goods between your islands but also sell or buy to rivals and traders. You can even transfer goods between different provinces.
You need at least one ship on a trade route but you can also assign multiple ships of you need to transport a large quantity of good. A trade route can also pass through multiple island in order to optimize the number of ships required and sometimes delivery time.
When setting up trade route you have option for each island like waiting for the exact number of goods or throwaway cargo if goods cannot be loaded. Using these option can help you preventing trade route issue or optimize your trade routes.

Fabius Gemellus Corvinus to Gnaeus Firmius Calidus.
A full and truthful account of the events leading to the end of the rebellion. Gaius Titanius Naso and household reached Whitecliff at the turning of the year.
Flares of illness kept him from speaking to public often, wife Titania passed on orders to subjects and servants. Probably gout — journey to Albion did not improve his health.
Shortly after imperial visit, Titanius contracted swamp fever. Knew it was going to kill him sooner or later. Titanius tried to negotiate with Celts, made plan and confided in wife Titania. Titanius died of fever shortly after ambush.
Since Celts let women speak in public, Titania was successful in negotiating ceasefire. No more attacks on supply ships, taxes punctual, many lives saved. Legion had no part in negotiations. We are obliged to her.
Post Scriptum: Titanius fond of wife, would not want her punished.

Youthful indiscretions are best forgotten, and I assure you that I have forgotten them. I am a man of virtue, now.
